text:
maria: heads up — gpu-monitor-bot alerted on node gpu-34: Xid 13 spikes + rising ECC corrected count. 6 Xid events in last 10m. anyone nearby? https://alerts.internal/redwood/alert/12345 :warning:

gpu-bot: Automated alert: Node=gpu-34, GPU0 Xid(13) occurrences=8, ECC_corrected=47 (previous=23). Logs uploaded: s3://redwood-gpu-logs/gpu-34/1913249812/ :robot_face:

jon: on it. can you paste dmesg + journalctl nvidia logs and `nvidia-smi -q` memory section? also kernel + driver versions?

maria: kernel=5.15.0-99-generic, nvidia-driver=530.41.03
Here are quick snippets: 
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (13): 0x79ff0007  MMU faults
[ 1235.001200] NVRM: GPU 0000:65:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus
```
journalctl: 
```
Mar 18 11:02:13 gpu-34 kernel: nvidia-modeset: GPU0: Uncorrectable ECC error detected
Mar 18 11:02:14 gpu-34 kernel: nvidia 0000:65:00.0: Xid (13): 0x79ff0007
```
`nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY` excerpt: 
```
GPU 0
    FB Memory Usage
        Total                       : 24576 MiB
        Used                        : 2048 MiB
        Free                        : 22528 MiB
ECC errors (detailed)
    Volatile
        Single-bit ECC errors       : 45
        Double-bit ECC errors       : 2
```

lee: hmm corrected ECC climbing then a few uncorrectable. could be flaky card or thermals. are we seeing similar across node rack-7? any recent firmware/driver rollouts?

ashley: quick triage commands i run for these: 
```
sudo journalctl -k -o cat | grep -i -E "NVRM|Xid" > /tmp/gpu-34-kernel.log
sudo journalctl -u nvidia-persistenced --since "15 minutes ago" -o cat > /tmp/gpu-34-nvidia.log
dmesg --ctime | grep -i NVRM > /tmp/gpu-34-dmesg.log
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,serial,driver_model,vbios_version --format=csv -q > /tmp/gpu-34-smi.csv
```
and a one-liner to summarize Xid codes: 
```
grep -o "Xid (13)\|Xid (31)\|Xid (43)" /tmp/gpu-34-kernel.log | sort | uniq -c
```

jon: for ingestion into our loghook/fast-parse pipeline i'd recommend a simple regex rule: `(?P<gpu>GPU\d+).*Xid \((?P<xid>\d+)\): (?P<desc>.*)` then attach `node=gpu-34, kernel=5.15.0-99, driver=530.41.03, serial=<from nvidia-smi>` as envelope metadata. capture ECC counters from `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC` too.

ashley: +1. also add `severity` heuristics: xid 13 + uncorrectable ECC -> severity=pgpu_hardware. For quick attribution we should tag by `vbios_version` and `gpu_serial` so we can correlate manufacturing/firmware batches. Example grok: `NVRM: GPU %{GREEDYDATA:gpu}: Xid \(%{NUMBER:xid}\): %{GREEDYDATA:rest}`

maria: i'm about to cordon and drain the node to reduce blast radius. scheduled now. `kubectl cordon gpu-34` then `kubectl drain gpu-34 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — it's running some long tests though, might need eviction grace. thoughts? :thinking_face:

lee: prefer cordon first (prevent new pods) then evict lower-priority pods slowly. if we see more uncorrectable ECC or fallback to GPU reset failures, mark node for replacement. set node label `needs-replace=true`.

jon: one more check: compare vbios across cards on node and siblings: `nvidia-smi -q | grep -i VBIOS` — mismatched vbios has bitten us before. could also be power-cycling issue, check BMC logs for slot 7.

maria: nvidia-smi shows two different vbios versions on gpu-34 (vbios: 90.04.8c.00 vs 90.04.8b.00). i'll include that in the ticket. uploading full logs to s3 now and will tag with `xid=13` and `ecc_corrected_increase` :arrow_up_small:

gpu-bot: Action taken: node gpu-34 cordoned by maria at 11:05. Eviction started. Incident ticket created: INC-2026-447.

ashley: followup suggestion — add a lightweight journald filter to our node-agent that extracts any `NVRM`/`Xid` lines and forwards them with envelope fields (node, gpu_index, serial, xid, vbios, driver). that'll drop our mean-time-to-attribute a lot. also add alert rate-limiter so one noisy job doesn't spam.

jon: i'll open a PR for the loghook regex, tests, and a sample dashboard panel for ECC rate + recent Xid events per node. planning to add aggregation by vbios and serial.

maria: thanks everyone. if we replace the card i'll file a postmortem and link hardware RMA ticket. tagging @lee @jon @ashley for followups. :thumbsup:

lee: ack, monitoring the drain and watching for additional Xid occurrences.

(reacts: maria :thumbsup:, jon :eyes:)
